question: Which article of the Indian Constitution mentions that "There shall be a High Court for each State"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 214**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Article 214** of the **Indian Constitution** states that "There shall be a High Court for each State." 
• The article ensures the establishment of a High Court as the highest judicial authority at the state level, responsible for administering justice within its territorial jurisdiction. 
• It provides the framework for the existence of a High Court in each state, although Parliament has the power to establish a common High Court for two or more states as per **Article 231**. 
• High Courts in India have jurisdiction over matters such as civil, criminal, constitutional, and administrative law, among others, within their respective states. 
• Each High Court is headed by a Chief Justice, and its composition and appointment procedures are governed by the Constitution of India. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Article 124:** 
• This article deals with the establishment and composition of the **Supreme Court of India**. 
• The Supreme Court is the apex judicial body in India, and its primary role is to act as a guardian of the Constitution. 
• It comprises the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and other judges as determined by Parliament. 
• **Article 226:** 
• Under this article, High Courts have the power to issue writs (such as habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari) for the enforcement of fundamental rights and for any other purpose. 
• This article empowers High Courts to ensure that the rule of law is upheld within their respective jurisdictions. 
• **Article 32:** 
• This article provides the right to constitutional remedies, allowing individuals to directly approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of fundamental rights. 
• It is often referred to as the "heart and soul" of the Indian Constitution, as described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. 
• **High Courts in India:** 
• The **Calcutta High Court**, established in **1862**, is the oldest High Court in India. 
• As of **2023**, there are **25 High Courts** in India, including common High Courts for some states and union territories. 
• For example, the High Court of Punjab and Haryana is a common High Court for these two states and the union territory of Chandigarh. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Role of High Courts:** 
• High Courts are responsible for overseeing subordinate courts, including district courts, within their jurisdiction. 
• They also have the authority to hear appeals from lower courts and provide remedies for violations of legal and constitutional rights. 
• **Appointment of Judges:** 
• Judges of the High Courts are appointed by the President of India in consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the respective state, and sometimes other judges of the High Court. 
• The qualifications for appointment include being a citizen of India and having at least **10 years** of experience as an advocate or a judicial officer. 
• **Jurisdiction of High Courts:** 
• They have **original jurisdiction** in matters like fundamental rights and election disputes. 
• They also have **appellate jurisdiction** over civil and criminal cases decided by subordinate courts. 
• **Significance of Article 214:** 
• This article ensures the decentralized administration of justice by establishing High Courts in states, making access to justice more efficient and localized. </ul
